summary: A hexagonal wooden tower on a red sandstone cliff at Île du Havre-Aubert, lit in 1871 and deactivated in 2011, with the Cormier family's keepers.

structures.note: Register gives 17.1 m; LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 54 ft (16.5 m)
Register: dates from the time the light was built

access.note: Conflicting: LighthouseFriends 'Grounds open, tower closed' but access to the property is not allowed because the keeper's house is in private hands; Rowlett 'Site open, tower closed', owner/site manager Canadian Coast Guard; Route des phares lists the manager as 'privé' (undated); the Quebec register says the tower is not open to visitors in summer.

events.note: Contract to Carrol and Sinclair ($4,600); total cost $6,828.01; construction 1870 to 1871 (Quebec register)
William Cormier lit the light for the first time, 30 June 1871 (LighthouseFriends)
Four wire stays sent to steady the tower
Inspection found two lamps and reflectors in very bad order after the lamps caught fire
Mammoth flat-wick lamps replaced circular-wick lamps
Inspectors Anderson and Smith judged the placement of the island lights ill-chosen (as quoted by LighthouseFriends)
New keeper's house built; original demolished the following year (1952)
Opened for three days, 26 to 28 September 2003, during Journées de la culture; more than 600 visitors
Cited as heritage property by the municipality of Les Îles-de-la-Madeleine, 17 January 2006
Lighthouse and keeper's house moved northwest across the road; Rowlett gives 2012 to 2014 to escape cliff erosion
Quebec register: by tradition, William Cormier's son Charles took over in 1912 (LighthouseFriends gives 1911)
Keeper's house sold to a private owner (Quebec register)

corrections.why: 17.1 m is the tower height (the register gives it as the tower's height). LighthouseFriends gives the focal plane as 107 feet, about 32.6 m, from the 1871 description; check against the current Coast Guard list before use.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's first year is 1871 (Rowlett, LighthouseFriends, Quebec register). The register gives 1870 to 1871 for construction, and LighthouseFriends gives 30 June 1871 for the first lighting; the story uses 1871.
LighthouseFriends gives 1911 for Charles Cormier's start; the Quebec register says that, by tradition, he took over in 1912. The story states both and does not settle it.

LighthouseFriends and Rowlett: Canadian Coast Guard owns and manages the site (Rowlett: site open, tower closed); Route des phares: manager 'privé' (undated); the keeper's house is private. The story states the sources and that the current owner is not confirmed.

Hexagonal in the Canadian and Quebec registers, LighthouseFriends, Rowlett and most of the Route des phares page; one sentence of the Route des phares page calls it octagonal. The story says hexagonal and notes the sentence.

notes_for_editor: NAMING: the record's 'Anse-à-la-Cabane' is the same lighthouse as LighthouseFriends' 'Île du Havre-Aubert (Amherst Island)' and Rowlett's 'Île du Havre-Aubert (L'Anse à la Cabane, Amherst Island, Cap du Sud)'. The Quebec register's other names include Amherst Lighttower, Phare de l'île du Havre-Aubert and Phare de Millerand. 'Amherst Island' is the English name for Île du Havre-Aubert (not the Ontario island). DISAGREEMENTS STATED IN THE STORY: (1) Tower shape: hexagonal (Canadian and Quebec registers, LighthouseFriends, Rowlett, Route des phares) against one octagonal sentence in the Route des phares page; French Wikipedia not cited. (2) Tower height: 17.1 m (Quebec register; French Canadian register) against 54 ft / 16.5 m (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett). (3) Charles Cormier's start: 1911 (LighthouseFriends) against 1912 by tradition (Quebec register). (4) Status and owner: the Quebec register (2009 to 2010 inventory) and the Route des phares page describe the light as still in operation; LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give deactivation in December 2011. Owner: Canadian Coast Guard (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett) against manager 'privé' (Route des phares, undated). NOT SETTLED AND NOT IN THE STORY: (5) First lighting: LighthouseFriends 30 June 1871; the French Wikipedia article gives 7 July 1871 (Wikipedia not cited). (6) Relocation: Rowlett gives 2012 to 2014 and a move northwest across the road; French Wikipedia gives autumn 2013 and a move of 75 m north (not cited). (7) Focal height: LighthouseFriends' 107 ft focal plane (about 32.6 m) against the record's 17.1 m, which is the tower height. The correction is proposed for a human to check against the current Coast Guard list, not applied. (8) The 1970 automation is from the Quebec register's text (not from LighthouseFriends). (9) Lantern material: the French register and the Quebec register give cast iron (fonte); the English register says steel. The story says cast iron, from the Quebec register. (10) The 2006 municipal citation and the 2012 nomination: the 2012 result was due by June 2015 (LighthouseFriends); the result is not found in the sources read. ROSTER: keepers come from LighthouseFriends' 'Keepers' line; the Quebec register lists the same three names without years. The Department's statement for the year ended 30 June 1901 has 'Cormier, Wm Amherst Island' (scan p. 255, printed p. 144) and the image shows the appointment date 26 April 1871 and salary $300 on the same row; both were checked on the page image. Charles Cormier's and Boudreau's tenures come from LighthouseFriends alone, and the Quebec register gives Charles 1912. STORMS AND WRECKS: no wreck or storm was tied to this light in the sources read; the 200 wrecks are for the islands as a whole. The Quebec register gives more than 700 shipwrecks for the region over the years. The 1890 inspection is quoted as LighthouseFriends quotes it; the original report was not located in the corpus (which covers Canadian reports to 1923-24 only as Marine branch reports). The keeper's house in the record is the 1951 house, not the 1871 one. No newspaper search was run for this Canadian station. General period context: not used. No photos added. The grounds_open flag was removed because the sources conflict (see access note).
